newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil steady despite crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil steady despite crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps weakened slightly at midday on Wednesday despite large overnight falls to crude prices as the market counted on sustained local physical buying support to shore prices up, traders said.
"The physical purchases is keeping the gas oil market steady despite the big drop in crude," one trader said.
June gas oil swaps were last quoted at $24.75-$24.85 per barrel range, down about 10 cents from Tuesday, while July was quoted down five cents at $24.80-$24.90, brokers said.
June traded earlier in the day at $24.80 and July traded at $24.85 per barrel, they said.
Traders said the market's resilience despite an overnight 78 cents drop in July Brent crude prices to $19.22 per barrel was due mainly to sustained buying from a small group of traders.
The traders on Tuesday bought three 150,000-barrel cargoes at $25.00 and $25.10 per barrel free-on-board Singapore, up 20 and 30 cents above Monday's traded level.
The same traders also bought aggressively June and July paper late last week totalling up to two million barrels, traders said.
As a resulted of their purchases, prices have held steady at around the $25.00 mark over the past month despite a deluge of sellers in the physical market.
Over the past week, up to 10 cargoes have been offered daily with between one and four cargoes traded per day.
And despite the daily trades more sellers have emerged as players who have not been able to offload their arbitrage cargoes look to these traders to pick up the barrels.
June fuel oil was last quoted down about 75 cents from Tuesday at $99.00/$100.00 per tonne, brokers said. The weaker prices were due to both poor demand and the big drop to crude prices.
